phases.name: Concept
phases.goal: Decide what the game is, and what it is not, before writing code.

gates.text: One-sentence pitch and 3 design pillars written (docs/GDD.md)
Scope ladder written: must / should / could / won't, sized to your weekly hours
Decided up front, in docs/decisions/: multiplayer or not, saves, languages, accessibility, target platforms and input devices (bolted on late, these cost the most)
Market check: 3 comparable games, what yours does differently, who plays it
Game name searched before a logo or store page: the web, Steam and the trademark databases where it will sell (any video game with the same or a similar name conflicts; godot-legal)
Kill criteria for the prototype written down (e.g. 'a stranger doesn't ask for a second run')

phases.name: Prototype
phases.goal: Prove the core loop is fun with the ugliest possible build.

gates.text: Project builds and the suite is wired in (godot-ci init)

Trailer script written before the game is built (docs/TRAILER.md): the genre clear in the first 5 seconds, then the hook, content last; three standout moments; every core mechanic with the on-screen feedback that shows a viewer the player caused it
Core loop is playable from the main scene
Two or three variants of the core action built cheaply and one chosen by playing them, not by argument
A stranger played 15 minutes unprompted and you watched what they did
Verdict recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md: PROCEED, PIVOT or KILL

phases.name: Vertical slice
phases.goal: One polished, representative slice that runs end to end: menu, play, save, quit.

gates.text: A test framework is chosen and tests run in CI (godot-ci detect lists a test runner)
An export preset exists and godot-ci export -Run passes
Automation flags exist and work in an export: --seed reproduces a run, --autoplay plays it, --no-save protects the player's save (godot-automation-hooks)
Menu, one full level/encounter, UI and save/load work together
Every screen screenshotted at the target resolution and one other aspect ratio, and reviewed (godot-ci.ps1 shot)
Game feel pass: input, feedback, audio and juice on the core action
Tech debt listed in docs/TECH-DEBT.md: every system the slice hacked, stubbed or never started, the work it needs at the size of the whole game, and the total you accept

Frame budget met on the busiest slice scene filled as the finished game will be (draw distance, level of detail, crowds, effects), not on showcase assets: godot-ci.ps1 bench -Scene <that scene> -BudgetMs <budget> passes

Slice verdict recorded: PROCEED, PIVOT or KILL. PROCEED only if it plays as the intended experience (not a feature list or a tech demo), core gameplay is settled and the tech debt fits; otherwise take more slice time. Scope ladder re-sized from real velocity

phases.name: Production
phases.goal: Build the rest as a series of playable milestones, cutting scope (never testing) when one slips.

gates.text: Milestones listed in docs/MILESTONES.md, each a playable build 2-6 weeks apart
All 'must' scope items implemented
Bot balance runs: a bot with human-like error plays every encounter headless over several seeds; lengths and difficulty hit their targets
A bot reaches the ending on every CI run (the playthrough runner: playthrough.json lists the milestones), so no build ships that nobody finished
Every fixed bug has a regression test
Feature freeze: no new features, only the existing list gets finished

phases.name: Alpha and beta
phases.goal: Stabilise: bugs, balance, performance, accessibility, localisation. No new features.

gates.text: Alpha: every feature exists end to end, even if rough; internal playthrough done
Closed playtest with 5+ people you don't know; top issues triaged
At least one change-and-replay round after the alpha: what playtesters struggled with was redesigned, not only bug-fixed, and played again
Worst case benchmarked (godot-ci.ps1 bench): p99 within budget with V-Sync on and off, at the target resolution, zero GC collections in the frame loop; also checked on minimum-spec hardware
Accessibility basics: rebindable input, readable text, no colour-only cues
Every shipped language played start to end by a native speaker who had not played the game (one language: done when it ships)
Full suite green with a coverage floor you chose

phases.name: Release candidate and launch
phases.goal: Ship it, from a clean export, with a page people could find.

gates.text: Store page live ('Coming soon'), at least 2 weeks before release on Steam and ideally months: capsules at the current sizes (doctor checks store/steam), gameplay trailer, 5+ screenshots, tags
Demo build tested on a clean machine
Gold master: release build exported by CI, launched with export -Run, no engine errors
The release is exactly the build that was tested: tagged in git, source and build archived together
Credits and third-party notices built from assets.json (credits command), reachable from the main menu
Privacy policy published if the game sends any data (telemetry, accounts, online play); Google Play and the App Store want one in every case
Age ratings: Steam's content survey (Germany and Indonesia need its ratings), IARC for other stores
End-user licence (or the store's own terms) and refund rules checked; copyright and trademark registration decided (godot-legal)
Tagged GitHub release created from CI; builds uploaded to the store

phases.name: Post-launch
phases.goal: Fix what players hit, listen, then decide what the next game or update is.

gates.text: Day-one hotfix path rehearsed (tag, CI export, upload)
First two weeks of feedback and crash reports triaged
Retrospective written: what to repeat, what to stop (docs/RETRO.md)
